segments.source: An undisturbed archaeological site has four layers from top to bottom: A, B, C, D. In an undisturbed sequence, lower layers were deposited earlier. D contains an object dated 1300, C contains one dated 1450, and B contains one dated 1600. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 3 km and two checkpoints are 2 cm apart.
Rules.

In an undisturbed sequence, a lower layer is older than a layer above it. A securely dated object provides a constraint on the layer that contains it, but one object does not date every other object exactly. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Which is older, Layer C or Layer B? Can the exact year of deposition of Layer A be deduced? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.

1. C lies below B, so C is older than B by the stratigraphic rule. 2. No exact dated object or deposition year is given for A. 3. Therefore only relative ordering, not an exact year for A, is justified. Cross-domain check: 2×3=6 km.
Answer.
Layer C is older than Layer B. The exact deposition year of Layer A cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 6 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
Relative dating and absolute dating answer different questions and should not be confused.
Formal model.
Partial order from vertical position plus numeric constraints from dated objects.
Problem 337. Reading an archaeological sequence: case 2
Knowledge context.
Archaeological layers provide relative chronological information. Dates from objects add constraints but do not automatically make every date exact.
Given facts.

An undisturbed archaeological site has four layers from top to bottom: A, B, C, D. In an undisturbed sequence, lower layers were deposited earlier. D contains an object dated 1305, C contains one dated 1465, and B contains one dated 1620. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 8:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.

In an undisturbed sequence, a lower layer is older than a layer above it. A securely dated object provides a constraint on the layer that contains it, but one object does not date every other object exactly. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Which is older, Layer C or Layer B? Can the exact year of deposition of Layer A be deduced? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. C lies below B, so C is older than B by the stratigraphic rule. 2. No exact dated object or deposition year is given for A. 3. Therefore only relative ordering, not an exact year for A, is justified. Cross-domain check: 8+2=10, so the team finishes at 10:00.
Answer.
Layer C is older than Layer B. The exact deposition year of Layer A cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 10:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Relative dating and absolute dating answer different questions and should not be confused.
Formal model.
Partial order from vertical position plus numeric constraints from dated objects.
Problem 338. Reading an archaeological sequence: case 3

D contains an object dated 1310, C contains one dated 1480, and B contains one dated 1640. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 13 members, requires at least 7 present for quorum, and 11 are present.
Rules.

In an undisturbed sequence, a lower layer is older than a layer above it. A securely dated object provides a constraint on the layer that contains it, but one object does not date every other object exactly. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Task.
